_how: First draft written by the local qwen2.5:14b model (sovereign-first: prose drafting runs on the estate's own GPU), then edited so every mitigation is concrete and every 'known' is a measured fact from fallfloor.

risks.risk: The small models on the laptops answer wrongly and nobody notices (fallfloor measured 52% silently wrong on support).
risks.mitigation: Customer-facing output stays assisted: an agent approves every reply, and the go/no-go board blocks unsupervised sending until measured evidence clears the policy threshold.
risks.owner: AI platform lead, with the head of customer operations

risks.risk: Spam screening over-flags legitimate messages (fallfloor: 18 of 92 wrongly flagged).
risks.mitigation: No automatic quarantine; flags go to a person, and Phase 1 re-measures on the bank's own messages with enough spam items to trust the catch rate.

risks.risk: A laptop's GPU faults mid-run (seen during fallfloor's development on an Intel Iris Xe with a 2023 driver).
risks.mitigation: Work queues persist on the node; a faulted node is restarted and resumes; the desk moves work off a dead node; driver updates go through device policy.

risks.risk: The laptops are slower than the fitted rates on the bank's own documents, so the floor needs more hours.
risks.mitigation: Phase 1 measures the real seconds per item; the floor has headroom at the planned enrolment and more laptops can be enrolled — still no new hardware.

risks.risk: An enrolled laptop is lost or stolen with queued work on it.
risks.mitigation: Full-disk encryption and device policy on every enrolled laptop; queues hold only the work in flight and are cleared on completion; the desk reassigns work from a node that has gone.

risks.risk: Tampered or wrong model weights reach the nodes.
risks.mitigation: Weights enter only through the one outbound door into a hash-pinned internal mirror; nodes refuse a model whose hash is not on the approved list.

risks.risk: A model's licence does not allow commercial use (fallfloor's 3B comparison model is research-licensed).
risks.mitigation: Only Apache 2.0 or equivalent licences in production; the licence is recorded in the AI system register before a model is approved.

risks.risk: The law moves again (the Digital Omnibus already moved the AI Act's high-risk dates; UK Articles 22A–22D are new).
risks.mitigation: Quarterly legal check of the compliance map against the primary texts; the design keeps high-risk uses out of the rollout.

risks.risk: The team cannot run it: inference, security and on-call are in-house skills.
risks.mitigation: A team of three from day one (the same size the corporate model needs), runbooks from the pilot, and the corporate route kept as a fallback for any workload that fails its gate.
